Case p^8: 2^8 = 256 ≤ 1000, 3^8 = 6561 > 1000, so only 256. Case p^2 q^2 = (pq)^2 with p < q primes: need pq ≤ 31. The products of two distinct primes up to 31 are 6, 10, 14, 15, 21, 22, 26, giving squares 36, 100, 196, 225, 441, 484, 676. Total: 256 + 36 + 100 + 196 + 225 + 441 + 484 + 676 = 2414.
